```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", dev = "png", dpi = 110)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(patchwork)
  library(scales); library(knitr)
})
ROOT <- ".."
DAT  <- file.path(ROOT, "report", "data")
theme_umap <- theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 11),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"), legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))

umap_cat <- function(d, col, title = col, pal = NULL, size = 0.3, highlight = NULL, size_hi = 1.1) {
  d <- d[order(d[[col]] %in% highlight), ]
  d$.sz <- ifelse(d[[col]] %in% highlight, size_hi, size)
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = .data[[col]], size = .sz)) +
    geom_point(stroke = 0, shape = 16) + scale_size_identity() + ggtitle(title) + theme_umap +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3), title = NULL))
  if (!is.null(pal)) p <- p + scale_colour_manual(values = pal)
  p
}
umap_gene <- function(d, g, title = g, size = 0.3, size_hi = 1.1) {
  d <- d[order(d[[g]]), ]
  d$.sz <- ifelse(d[[g]] > 0, size_hi, size)
  ggplot(d, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = .data[[g]], size = .sz)) +
    geom_point(stroke = 0, shape = 16) + scale_size_identity() + ggtitle(title) + theme_umap +
    scale_colour_gradientn(colours = c("grey88", "#fdae61", "#d73027", "#67001f"), name = NULL)
}
PAL_CALL <- c(gdT = "#b2182b", `TRDC+_CD4CD8B` = "#4393c3", `TRDC+_NKlike` = "#984ea3",
              `TRDC+_CD3neg` = "#92c5de", non_gd = "grey85")
```

um   <- read.csv(gzfile(file.path(DAT, "tnk_umap.csv.gz")), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

                 check.names = FALSE)

                               gregexpr("[0-9.]+(?= %)", grep("TRAC=TRBC1=TRBC2=0", log06, value = TRUE), perl = TRUE))[[1]])
tl    <- nksub[nksub$`T-like` %in% c(TRUE, "True"), ]

# Summary

* **Question.** Can γδ T cells be identified in the Klughammer metastatic breast cancer atlas
  (10x 3', no TCR sequencing), as was done for Azizi et al. 2018?
* **Answer: not among the cells annotated as T.** In this dataset TRDC — the only γδ marker that is
  detected — is **more frequent in cells that are certainly αβ T cells (CD4⁺ or CD8B⁺) than in γδ
  candidates**, at every sequencing depth and in 21/22 patients. The same test cleanly separates γδ from
  αβ cells in Azizi, where the TCR provides the truth. The same holds for a T-like subpopulation found among cells annotated as NK (see below).
* **TRDV genes are not detected** (≤ 0.4 % of TRDC⁺ cells), so Vδ1/Vδ2 subsets cannot be studied either.
* **Ambient-RNA correction (decontX) and alternative markers (TRGC1, TRGC2, TRGV9, combinations) do not
  rescue the signal.**
* **Implication.** Any γδ annotation of this atlas based on TRDC (including automated annotators) would
  consist mostly of αβ T cells.
* **Open point (follow-up, Section 5).** The expression rule excluded cells with NK markers, and the
  background test used only cells annotated as T, so the cells annotated as NK were never evaluated as
  possible γδ cells. Re-clustering them reveals **`r sum(tl$n)` cells (`r percent(sum(tl$n) / 3496, 1)` of NK, present in at least `r max(tl$patients)` patients)
  with T-cell transcripts**. They are not NK+T doublets (UMI content of a single cell), and inside them
  TRDC/TRGC are at least as frequent in CD8B⁺ (αβ) cells as in CD8B⁻ cells: no γδ signal, as in the T cells.
* **Combined constant-region rule** (TRDC/TRGC⁺, TRAC/TRBC⁻, CD3E⁺, CD4⁻): it does not work, because
  γδ cells validated by TCR also express TRAC/TRBC (Section 5.4).
* Studying γδ cells with clinical association requires a dataset with TCR data, e.g. **Bassez et al.
  2021** (5' + TCR, ~30 patients, anti-PD-1 response).

# Data

```{r cohort}
clin %>% transmute(Patient = patient, Assay = assay, `Biopsy site` = site_biopsy,
                   Receptors = receptors_biopsy, Subtype = subtype, Stage = stage_at_diagnosis,
                   Presentation = metastatic_presentation, Age = age, `T cells` = n_T, `NK cells` = n_NK) %>%
  kable(caption = "Patients with T/NK cells (28 of 30; one metastatic biopsy each). Subtype from biopsy receptors: HER2+ if HER2+; HR+ if ER+ or PR+ (incl. PR-low); otherwise TNBC.")
```

T/NK cells as annotated by the authors (`author_cell_type` = T or NK; `r format(nrow(um), big.mark = ",")`
cells), raw counts from the CELLxGENE release; Harmony (by patient) + Leiden for the embedding.

# Approach

Without TCR data, γδ cells must be identified from expression alone. The rule was **calibrated on the
Azizi 10x data**, where the TCR tells which TRDC⁺ cells are γδ (no productive αβ pair).

**Cells included.** Both cells annotated as T and cells annotated as NK were included, because γδ cells
share a cytotoxic programme with NK cells and could have been annotated as NK.

**Positive marker: why TRDC.** Every TCR gene that could mark γδ cells was considered (details in the
Azizi report, Appendix A.4, where the TCR gives an independent truth):

* **TRDV1/TRDV2/TRDV3** — the most direct markers in 5' data (TRDV2⁺ cells: 12 % αβ in Azizi), but
  essentially **not detected in this 3' dataset** (≤ 0.4 % of TRDC⁺ cells; Section 4.1).
* **TRAC/TRBC1/TRBC2 as negative markers** — γδ cells transcribe them (81 %, 70 %, 79 % in Azizi γδ
  cells), and cells without TRAC/TRBC transcripts are mostly αβ cells with a productive αβ pair (74 %),
  i.e. dropout (Section 5.4).
* **TRGC1/TRGC2** — mostly transcribed by αβ cells: 68 % and 78 % of TRGC1⁺/TRGC2⁺ cells in Azizi carry
  a productive αβ pair (TRDC⁺: 31 %).
* **TRDC** — the most specific constant-region gene and the only γδ gene detected here.

Constant-region markers and combinations, against the γδ call in Azizi and with the Klughammer
background test:

```{r positive}
pos %>% kable(caption = "γδ constant-region markers, alone and with the exclusion filters (CD3⁺ CD4⁻ CD8B⁻ KLRF1⁻ FCER1G⁻). Precision/recall against the TCR call in Azizi 10x; background ratio in Klughammer (Section 4.3; > 1 = γδ signal).")
```

* **TRGC1/TRGC2** are also transcribed by αβ T cells: alone, only 10–19 % of TRGC⁺ cells are γδ.
  Adding them to TRDC (TRDC *or* TRGC) raises recall but lowers precision from 0.88 to 0.55.
* Requiring **TRDC *and* TRGC** gives the highest precision (0.92) but loses most γδ cells (recall 0.27).
* TRDC was therefore the only positive marker. In Klughammer the choice does not change the conclusion:
  **every** marker or combination has a background ratio < 1.

**Exclusion criteria.**

* **TRAC/TRBC cannot be used** — true γδ cells express germline TRAC/TRBC at levels ≥ αβ cells
  (Section 5.4).
* **CD4 and CD8B** (CD8αβ) are almost absent from γδ cells (0 % and 4 % vs 31 % and 40 % in αβ cells) →
  used to exclude αβ cells.
* **KLRF1 and FCER1G** exclude NK cells, because TRDC is detected in 83 % of cells annotated as NK.
  *Limitation identified afterwards:* this filter was validated in Azizi 10x, which contains only sorted
  CD3⁺ T cells, so it could not reveal γδ cells with an NK phenotype. In Klughammer it reduces the cells
  annotated as NK that pass the rule from 1,279 to 29, i.e. it largely undoes the inclusion of NK cells
  (Section 5).

```{r rule}
rule %>% kable(caption = "Expression rules: precision/recall against the TCR-based call in Azizi 10x, and cells passing each rule in Klughammer. The final rule gives 88 % precision in Azizi and selects 3.9 % of Klughammer T cells.")
```

# Results

## TRDV genes are not detected; TRDC is widespread

```{r detection}
det %>% rename(`% of author T cells` = T, `% of author NK cells` = NK) %>%
  kable(caption = "Detection (> 0 UMI) of TCR and lineage genes.")
```

* TRDV1/TRDV2/TRDV3 are essentially absent (3' chemistry captures the constant region) → no Vδ subsets.
* TRDC is detected in **83 % of NK cells** and **14 % of T cells** — far above the
  expected γδ frequency (2.7 % in Azizi 10x).
* **CD3E is detected in 34.7 % of cells annotated as NK.** This is analysed in Section 5.1–5.2: part of it
  is not explained by T-cell transcripts, and part comes from a subpopulation with a T-cell profile.

## No γδ population emerges on the UMAP

```{r umap, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
(umap_cat(um, "author_cell_type", "Author label") | umap_gene(um, "TRDC", "TRDC expression") |
   umap_cat(um, "gd_call", "Expression-rule call", PAL_CALL, highlight = c("gdT"))) /
(umap_gene(um, "CD8B") | umap_gene(um, "KLRF1") | umap_gene(um, "TRGC2"))
```

In Azizi, γδ cells formed their own cluster (37 % γδ). Here, cells passing the rule are **scattered across
the T-cell compartment**; no Leiden cluster has more than 7 % of them.

Genes **not** used in the rule are only modestly enriched in the called cells, much less than in true γδ
cells in Azizi:

```{r validation}
val %>% rename(Gene = 1) %>%
  kable(caption = "% detection of genes not used in the rule. Klughammer calls vs TRDC⁻ T cells, and TCR-validated γδ vs αβ cells in Azizi 10x.")
```

## Background test: TRDC is not γδ-specific in this dataset

If TRDC marked γδ cells, it should be much more frequent among **γδ candidates** (T cells, CD3⁺, CD4⁻
CD8B⁻, no NK markers) than among **sure αβ cells** (CD4⁺ or CD8B⁺). The ratio candidates/αβ is the key
number (> 1 = γδ signal):

```{r bg_table}
bg %>% transmute(Data = data, Marker = marker, `% in sure-αβ`, `% in DN candidates`,
                 `Ratio DN/αβ` = `ratio DN/αβ`) %>%
  kable(caption = "Background test for several markers. Azizi 10x (5', TCR-validated) is the positive control.")
```

* In **Azizi**, TRDC is 5× more frequent in candidates (and TRDC + TRGC 10×): the test works.
* In **Klughammer**, every marker has a ratio **< 1**: TRDC, TRGC1, TRGC2 and their combinations are
  *more* frequent in sure αβ cells. TRGC1/2 are not γδ-specific even in Azizi.

**Not a sequencing-depth artefact.** Sure-αβ cells have more UMIs (CD4/CD8B are easier to detect in deeper
cells), so the comparison was repeated within UMI-depth bins:

```{r depth, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
dep %>% pivot_longer(c(`sure-αβ`, `DN candidates`), names_to = "group", values_to = "pct") %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(bin), pct, fill = group)) + geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~dataset, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`sure-αβ` = "#4393c3", `DN candidates` = "#b2182b")) +
  labs(x = "UMI-depth quintile (1 = shallowest)", y = "% TRDC⁺", fill = NULL)
```

The pattern holds in every depth bin: candidates > αβ in Azizi, αβ > candidates in Klughammer.

**Per patient** (≥ 30 cells per group):

```{r per_patient, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
ct <- cor.test(bpp$`sure-αβ`, bpp$pct_NK, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
n_up <- sum(bpp$`DN candidates` > bpp$`sure-αβ`)
p1 <- ggplot(bpp, aes(`sure-αβ`, `DN candidates`, colour = assay)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  coord_equal() + labs(x = "% TRDC⁺ in sure-αβ", y = "% TRDC⁺ in DN candidates", colour = NULL,
                       title = "Below the diagonal = no γδ signal") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
p2 <- ggplot(bpp, aes(pct_NK, `sure-αβ`, colour = assay)) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "% NK cells in T/NK", y = "% TRDC⁺ in sure-αβ", colour = NULL,
       title = sprintf("Spearman ρ = %.2f, p = %.3f", ct$estimate, ct$p.value)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
p1 + p2
```

* `r n_up` of `r nrow(bpp)` patients show more TRDC in candidates than in αβ cells.
* The TRDC background in αβ cells **increases with the NK content** of the sample and is higher with the
  3' v2 chemistry, which points to ambient RNA from NK cells; germline transcription of the TRA/TRD locus in
  αβ cells may also contribute. The two cannot be separated here.

## Ambient-RNA correction (decontX) does not help

decontX (celda 1.26) was run per sample on the **whole atlas** (all 157,531 cells, author cell types as
clusters). Estimated contamination of T/NK cells was low (median `r sprintf("%.1f %%", 100 * median(um$decontX_contamination, na.rm = TRUE))`),
and TRDC was removed from only 40 of 6,522 TRDC⁺ cells. The background-test ratios are unchanged
(table above, "Klughammer decontX"). Because TRDC is part of both the T and NK expression profiles,
decontX treats it as native rather than ambient.

# Follow-up: cells annotated as NK and the combined constant-region rule

Added in October 2026 after review of the first version: (i) 34.7 % of cells annotated as NK express
CD3E; (ii) the cells annotated as NK were never evaluated as γδ (NK-marker filter, background test on
cells annotated as T); (iii) proposal of a combined score TRDC/TRGC1/TRGC2⁺, TRAC/TRBC1/TRBC2⁻,
CD3E⁺, CD4⁻.

## Where CD3E in NK-annotated cells comes from

If CD3E in a cell type came from T cells (ambient RNA, doublets, mislabelled T cells), it should come
with CD3D in the same proportion as in T cells.

```{r cd3e}
cd3e %>% filter(n >= 1000) %>% arrange(desc(CD3E)) %>%
  select(`Cell type` = cell_type, n, CD3E, CD3D, CD3G, TRAC, TRBC2, CD8B, CD247, KLRF1, `CD3E/CD3D`) %>%
  kable(caption = "% of cells with > 0 UMI, all author cell types with ≥ 1,000 cells (whole atlas, raw counts).")
```

```{r cd3e_noT}
cd3n %>% rename(`Cell type` = cell_type) %>%
  kable(caption = "Cells with none of CD3D, CD3G, TRAC, TRBC2, CD8B: % that express CD3E.")
```

* In T cells CD3E is detected somewhat less often than CD3D (ratio
  `r cd3e$"CD3E/CD3D"[cd3e$cell_type == "T"]`). In the other cell types, the little CD3E present (1–4 %) comes with
  CD3D in a similar proportion, as expected if it comes from T cells.
* In cells annotated as NK the pattern is different: **more CD3E than CD3D** (ratio
  `r cd3e$"CD3E/CD3D"[cd3e$cell_type == "NK"]`). If CD3E followed CD3D as in T cells, 22 % would be expected; 34.7 % is
  observed. Among NK cells with no other T-cell transcript, `r cd3n$"% CD3E+"[cd3n$cell_type == "NK"]` % express CD3E,
  versus ≤ 1 % in other cell types.
* So part of the CD3E in NK-annotated cells is **not explained by T-cell transcripts** in this dataset.

## NK-annotated cells with a T-cell profile

```{r nk_cd3e}
nkco %>% filter(!gene %in% c("CD3E")) %>%
  kable(caption = "CD3E⁺ vs CD3E⁻ cells annotated as NK (% > 0 UMI), with author T cells as reference.")
```

CD3E⁺ NK-annotated cells express more CD3D, CD3G, TRAC and CD8B than CD3E⁻ ones, so some T-like cells are
among them. NK-annotated cells were re-embedded and sub-clustered (Harmony by patient, Leiden 1.0):

```{r nk_umap, fig.width=12, fig.height=6.5}
nkum$T_like <- ifelse(nkum$T_like %in% c(TRUE, "True"), "T-like", "other")
(umap_cat(nkum, "nk_sub", "NK-annotated cells: subclusters") |
   umap_cat(nkum, "T_like", "T-like subclusters (CD3D > 50 %)", c(`T-like` = "#b2182b", other = "grey80"),
            highlight = "T-like") | umap_gene(nkum, "CD3D")) /
(umap_gene(nkum, "TRAC") | umap_gene(nkum, "TRGC1") | umap_gene(nkum, "CD8B"))
```

```{r nk_sub}
nksub %>% select(subcluster, n, patients, `median UMI`, CD3E, CD3D, CD3G, TRAC, TRDC, TRGC1, TRGC2,
                 CD8A, CD8B, CD5, IL7R, KLRF1, FCER1G, FCGR3A, `T-like`) %>%
  kable(caption = "Subclusters of NK-annotated cells (% > 0 UMI). T-like = CD3D detected in > 50 % of cells.")
```

```{r nk_ref}
nkref %>% mutate(across(-gene, ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
  mutate(`expected NK+T doublet` = ifelse(gene %in% c("n", "patients", "median UMI"), NA,
           round(100 * (1 - (1 - `NK other subclusters` / 100) * (1 - `author T CD8B+` / 100)), 1))) %>%
  kable(caption = "T-like subclusters vs the other NK-annotated cells, CD8B⁺ author T cells and TCR-validated γδ cells of Azizi 10x. 'Expected NK+T doublet': detection expected if each cell were an NK cell plus a CD8⁺ T cell.")
```

* **`r sum(tl$n)` cells** (`r percent(sum(tl$n) / 3496, 1)` of NK-annotated cells, in at least `r max(tl$patients)` patients) form T-like
  subclusters: CD3D, TRAC and CD8A in 40–70 % of cells, together with NK genes (KLRF1, FCER1G in ~85 %).
* They have more TRGC1 than the other NK cells and than CD8⁺ T cells, but about what an NK+T doublet would
  give. Their T-cell genes are below the doublet expectation, and they have more UMIs than other NK cells.
* They do **not** resemble the TCR-validated γδ cells of Azizi: KLRF1, FCER1G and FCGR3A are high (≤ 2 % in
  Azizi γδ) and IL7R and CD5 low (83 % and 25 % in Azizi γδ). However, Azizi 10x contains only sorted
  T cells, so it cannot show what NK-like γδ cells look like.
* They could be NK-like γδ cells, NK-like αβ CD8 cells (CD8B in ~27 %) or NK+T doublets (next section).

## Are the T-like NK cells doublets, and do they contain γδ cells?

**Scrublet** was run per 10x channel on the whole atlas (all cell types, raw counts; expected rate 0.8 %
per 1,000 cells; threshold 0.25).

```{r dbl}
dbg %>% kable(caption = "Scrublet doublet scores by group.")
```

Scrublet flags almost no doublets anywhere in the atlas (≤ 1.2 % in every cell type), probably because
the published data were already filtered; it is also known to be weak for doublets of similar cell types
such as NK + T. It is therefore not informative here. A more direct test: an NK+T doublet contains the
RNA of two cells, so its UMI count should be close to NK + T.

```{r umi}
umi %>% kable(caption = "Median UMI per cell in the same patient (patients with ≥ 10 cells per group).")
```

The T-like cells have about the same UMI content as the other NK cells of the same patient (median ratio
`r round(median(umi$"T-like" / umi$"NK other"), 2)`) and about half of the doublet expectation (ratio
`r round(median(umi$"T-like" / umi$"NK + T (doublet expectation)"), 2)`); they are below 75 % of the doublet expectation in
`r sum(umi$"T-like" < 0.75 * umi$"NK + T (doublet expectation)")` of `r nrow(umi)` patients.
**They are single cells**: NK-like T cells (or NK cells with T-cell transcripts), not doublets.

**γδ signal inside the T-like cells.** The background test of Section 4.3 was repeated within them:
CD8B⁺ cells are αβ; if the CD8B⁻ ones contained γδ cells, TRDC/TRGC should be more frequent there.

```{r nkbt}
nkbt %>% kable(caption = "T-like NK cells: CD8B⁺ (αβ) vs CD8B⁻, also restricted to cells with CD3D and TRAC (comparable T-cell transcript content).")
```

TRDC, TRDC ≥ 2 UMI and TRGC1/TRGC2 are **as frequent or more frequent in the CD8B⁺ (αβ) cells**, also
when both groups are restricted to CD3D⁺TRAC⁺ cells. As in the T cells, there is no detectable γδ signal:
γδ cells may exist among them, but they cannot be told apart from αβ cells with these genes.

## Combined constant-region rule

Rule proposed: TRDC/TRGC1/TRGC2 positive, TRAC/TRBC1/TRBC2 negative, CD3E high, CD4 negative. Tested
against the TCR truth in Azizi 10x:

```{r az_det}
azdet %>% rename(Gene = 1) %>%
  kable(caption = "Azizi 10x: detection in TCR-validated γδ cells vs cells with a productive αβ pair.")
```

```{r az_rules}
azrul %>% kable(caption = "Azizi 10x: rules vs the TCR call.")
```

* γδ cells validated by TCR **also express TRAC, TRBC1 and TRBC2** (germline transcription); only
  `r ab0[1]` % have all three at zero (`r ab0[2]` % of αβ cells). Requiring TRAC/TRBC negativity therefore
  recovers about 1 % of γδ cells.
* As a continuous score (mean z of TRDC, TRGC1, TRGC2 minus mean z of TRAC, TRBC1, TRBC2), the AUC
  for γδ vs αβ is `r auc_s`, versus `r auc_d` for TRDC alone.
* "CD3E high" cannot be applied in Klughammer: CD3E is detected with 1 UMI in 65 % of CD3E⁺ T cells
  (median 6 UMI in Azizi 5'), and requiring ≥ 2 UMI leaves 0 cells passing the rule.

In Klughammer, without using the author labels:

```{r k_rules}
kbg %>% select(-`Azizi ratio DN/CD8B+`) %>%
  mutate(`ratio DN/CD8B+` = ifelse(`% in CD8B+ (αβ)` == 0 & `% in CD4-CD8B-` > 0, "n/a (no CD8B⁺ cell can pass)",
                                   as.character(`ratio DN/CD8B+`))) %>%
  kable(caption = "Klughammer, all T/NK cells: cells passing each rule, how many are annotated as NK, and % in CD8B⁺ (αβ) vs CD4⁻CD8B⁻ cells. The CD4⁻CD8B⁻ group includes NK cells, so ratios > 1 here reflect NK cells.")
```

The few cells passing the combined rules are mostly NK-annotated (KLRF1⁺), consistent with the rule
selecting NK cells with germline TRDC rather than γδ cells.

**The combined score used directly as a call.** Among CD3E⁺ CD4⁻ cells, the cells with the highest score
(top 1–10 %) were called γδ, with the same procedure in Azizi (positive control) and Klughammer (all T/NK
cells, author labels not used). Background test as in Section 4.3, restricted to cells without NK
markers: % of CD8B⁺ (αβ) vs CD8B⁻ cells called.

```{r csc}
csc %>% kable(caption = "Combined-score call. Precision/recall against the TCR call (Azizi only).")
```

```{r csv}
csv_ %>% kable(caption = "Genes not in the score that differ between γδ and αβ cells in Azizi (% detected), in called cells without NK markers (top 3 %) vs the other CD3E⁺CD4⁻ cells without NK markers.")
```

* **In Azizi, the score selects mostly αβ cells** (precision 0.41 at the top 3 %, vs 0.88 for the TRDC rule)
  and fails the background test (ratio < 1): TRGC2, which αβ CD8 cells also transcribe, drives the top of
  the score. Ranking cells (AUC 0.83) is not the same as calling a rare population at the top.
* **In Klughammer, 55–78 % of the top-scoring cells are NK-annotated (KLRF1/FCER1G⁺)**, and among the
  others the background ratio is ≈ 1 (no γδ enrichment).
* The genes not in the score shift in the γδ direction (more KLRC1/TYROBP, less CD5/CD28) — but the same
  shift is seen in Azizi, where most called cells are αβ: it marks an NK-like/cytotoxic T-cell state, not
  γδ identity.

# Conclusions

* Among cells annotated as T, γδ T cells **cannot be reliably identified at single-cell level**: the only
  detectable γδ marker (TRDC) behaves as background, Vδ genes are not captured, and neither ambient-RNA
  correction, TRGC-based markers nor a combined constant-region score rescue the signal.
* Among cells annotated as NK there is a T-like subpopulation (`r sum(tl$n)` cells) that the first analysis did not
  evaluate. They are single cells (not NK+T doublets), and within them TRDC/TRGC show no γδ signal
  (as frequent in CD8B⁺ αβ cells as in CD8B⁻ cells). The conclusion therefore extends to the NK-annotated
  cells: γδ cells cannot be identified among them either.
* Consequently, **γδ abundance, phenotype or clinical associations should not be derived from this
  dataset**, and TRDC-based annotations of it should be treated with caution.
* The approach (calibration against TCR-validated cells + background test) is reusable to check the
  feasibility of γδ analysis in any 3' dataset before interpreting it.
* **Recommended next dataset**: Bassez et al. 2021 (Nat Med) — breast cancer, 10x 5' + TCR, ~30 patients
  before/on anti-PD-1 with expansion status and receptor subtype; processed counts and TCR clonotypes are
  available from the Lambrechts lab website.

# Methods

Scripts in `~/single_cell/Klughammer/gdT/`: `01_extract_TNK.py` (T/NK cells, raw counts, clinical table),
`02_process_TNK.py` (normalisation, HVG, PCA, Harmony, UMAP, Leiden), `03_gd_calling.py` (expression
rule and validation), `04a_export_for_decontx.py` / `04b_decontx.R` (conda env `decontx`) /
`04c_background_test.py` (ambient-RNA correction and background test), `05_export_for_report.py`.
Follow-up: `06_combined_rule_test.py` (positive-marker choice, combined constant-region rule, Azizi
TCR truth), `07_cd3e_by_celltype.py` (CD3E vs other T transcripts in every cell type of the atlas),
`08_nk_subclusters.py` (re-clustering of NK-annotated cells), `09_doublets.py` (Scrublet per channel,
UMI-based doublet test and background test inside the T-like NK cells), `10_combined_score_call.py`
(combined score used as a call in Azizi and Klughammer).
Calibration data: `~/single_cell/Azizi/` (Azizi et al. 2018, GSE114727, 10x 5' + TCR).
